description: Iterative outfit builder: each generate call REPLACES what the person wears on one body region with the uploaded item. The client must resend the ORIGINAL user photo plus the latest generated result as the new 'current photo' for the next item.

categories.name: Outfit Set (1 set lengkap)
categories.prompt: You are editing Image 2 (the CURRENT photo of the user) to dress the person in a COMPLETE OUTFIT SET. Image 1 is the user's ORIGINAL untouched photo — use it ONLY as a reference for the person's true face, identity, hairstyle, skin tone, and body proportions; ignore its clothing, pose, and background. Image 3 is an outfit reference (a flat-lay, lookbook, collage, or photo of a model) showing several clothing items and accessories together. First identify every wearable item in Image 3: tops and layers (e.g. shirt, cardigan, jacket, vest, tie), bottoms (pants, jeans, skirt, shorts), footwear, and accessories (e.g. watch, headphones, bag, hat, glasses, jewelry). IGNORE everything in Image 3 that is not a wearable item: text, item lists, labels, color palette swatches, watermarks, app buttons or icons, the background, and any model's face, hair, or body. REPLACE, DO NOT ADD: for every body region covered by an item in Image 3, REMOVE COMPLETELY what the person in Image 2 currently wears there and dress them in the item from Image 3, copying its exact shape, fit, length, color, pattern, material, and details. This includes the bottoms and footwear — do not change only the top. Reproduce the layering exactly as styled in Image 3 (e.g. shirt collar over or under the cardigan, tie inside the cardigan, top tucked in or untucked, how wide or cropped the pants are, and how the hem falls on the shoes). For body regions with NO item in Image 3, keep what the person in Image 2 currently wears unchanged. Wear accessories naturally and only those that actually appear in Image 3: a watch on the wrist, headphones resting around the neck (never covering the face or changing the hairstyle), a bag on the shoulder or in hand, a hat on the head, glasses on the face. If the new outfit reveals skin that was previously covered, render it realistically with the person's skin tone from Image 1. Keep the exact same face, hairstyle, pose, body proportions, and background as Image 2. Match the lighting, shadows, and color grading of the outfit to the rest of the photo so it looks like one cohesive, realistic photograph — do NOT convert to cartoon, anime, or illustration. Output one realistic photo with the exact same size, framing, and pose as Image 2. FINAL CHECK: (1) Is the face and identity from Image 1 preserved? (2) Is EVERY wearable item from Image 3 now worn by the person — including bottoms, shoes, and accessories, not only the top? (3) Are the old clothes on every replaced body region completely gone? (4) Is no text, label, color swatch, or button from Image 3 visible in the output? (5) Is the lighting and color grading consistent across the whole photo?
